entities.name: Nicholas Bubwith
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nicholas Bubwith (c.1355–1424) was an English bishop and royal administrator who served as Bishop of London (1406–1407), Bishop of Salisbury (1407–1408), and Bishop of Bath and Wells (1408–1424). A leading ecclesiastical administrator under Henry IV and Henry V, Bubwith combined Church leadership with royal service — the typical pattern of medieval bishop-administrators who served simultaneously as senior clerics and as key figures in royal governance. He attended the Council of Constance (1414–1418) — the Church council that ended the Western Schism by deposing multiple claimant popes and electing Martin V as the legitimate pope.

His attendance at Constance placed him at one of the most consequential Church councils of the medieval period.

He was also a benefactor of the Diocese of Bath and Wells — endowing almshouses and building projects.

He was a significant Lancastrian Church administrator.
